controls.name: C_counter_live
controls.must_fire_because: the hashlib substitution must actually reach node_hash/desc_hash; a counter that never incremented would report a flat verifier that is really an uninstrumented one
controls.can_fail_because: if TW.hashlib were bound at definition time, or verify called hashlib directly, every count stays 0
controls.null_must_contain: a run where every count is 0 or constant
controls.detail: distinct hash-call counts inside the verifier

controls.name: C_reject_corrupt
controls.must_fire_because: every counted verification must be doing real work: the good proof must verify TRUE and a corrupted copy must verify FALSE, or the numbers describe a function returning early (A29)
controls.can_fail_because: if the flipped sibling digest were unused by the fold, the corrupted proof would still verify
controls.null_must_contain: a verifier that accepts the corrupted proof, which would put corrupt_rejected at 0
controls.detail: both directions of the verifier, counted

controls.name: C_null_bounds_the_flat_case
controls.must_fire_because: the flat null must be FLAT and the real verifier must not be, or "not flat" is asserted against nothing (A20)
controls.can_fail_because: if flat_verify hashed the proof it would scale, and if the real verifier ignored the path it would match the null
controls.null_must_contain: a null whose work varies with proof size
controls.detail: flat null vs the real verifier over the sweep

controls.name: C_proof_size_varies
controls.must_fire_because: the x-axis must span a real range, or flatness in y is unreadable
controls.can_fail_because: if proof size were set by something the key count does not move, the sweep would be flat in x -- and on the three REAL sets it was, at 48.15% against this file's pre-registered 50% bar
controls.null_must_contain: a sweep whose proof sizes are all within a few percent
controls.detail: mean proof bytes across the sweep; spread 1423.9%

controls.name: C_components_disagree
controls.must_fire_because: verifier work has two load-free components -- bytes hashed and path steps -- and this control asks whether either one alone can stand for verify cost. It FIRES when they order the key sets differently, which means neither is a proxy and only a timed run could settle which dominates
controls.can_fail_because: bytes and steps could rise together across the three sets, as they do across the sweep
controls.null_must_contain: two components that order the sets identically, in which case either would be a usable proxy
controls.detail: three real sets ordered by hash bytes vs by path steps

controls.name: C_every_position_forced
controls.must_fire_because: the finding is that the verifier is FORCED to read the proof, not merely that it happens to hash that many bytes. Corrupting a sibling digest at EVERY path position, one at a time, must be rejected at every position
controls.can_fail_because: a verifier checking only the leaf, or only the final fold step, would accept corruption at earlier positions while hashing exactly the same number of bytes
controls.null_must_contain: a verifier that accepts a corruption at some position, i.e. one that hashes bytes whose value it does not depend on
controls.detail: one flipped sibling digest per path position, all proofs

falsifiers.name: F_verify_flat
falsifiers.can_fail_because: verifier hash-byte spread across the sweep is under 10% while proof-size spread is over 50%
falsifiers.null_must_contain: the flat_verify null, which does one hash regardless of proof size
falsifiers.refutes: that the S77->S80 branching-cost result matters to the job class at all: if the verifier pays the same whatever the proof size, only the prover pays and the branching model is a prover-side curiosity
falsifiers.fires_when: verifier hash-byte spread across the sweep is under 10% while proof-size spread is over 50%
falsifiers.verdict: survived — the falsifier did not fire

falsifier: verifier hash work flat (<10% spread) while proof size spans >50%
